competitors.what_they_have: The WHV community's reference dossier, four chapters (intro, TFN FAQs, how to apply step by step, using your TFN), a long comment thread with real applicant questions, and a visible modified date (Oct 2025). Strong on authority and links, weak on freshness and figures, and it does not cite ATO pages. This is the page to beat for the working holiday phrasing.

The current format benchmark: summary first, 'Who can apply', a 4 step how to apply, 'What to do when your TFN arrives' (5 actions), 'Where to find your TFN', 7 FAQs (processing time, cost, working before it arrives, applying from overseas, lost TFN), links to ATO and myGov, and 'Last updated July 2026'.

Key takeaways plus a short answer, a table of application paths (visa holder in Australia, citizen, overseas), 5 steps for visa holders, 'Started a job but your TFN hasn't arrived?', scam warning, an 'Authoritative sources' block, 4 FAQs, ATO phone numbers, updated date (Sep 2026). It states 47% as the no-TFN rate and the $18,200 tax-free threshold, both wrong for a working holiday maker: our dated 45% and 15% figures are the differentiator.

The official rule set (updated 22 June 2026): online application needs a work rights visa and you must be located in Australia, 417 and 462 listed by name, no documents to send, free, TFN posted to the Australian address within 28 days, do not apply again within 28 days, quote the receipt ID if it has not arrived. Our page currently states none of these in the ATO's own terms and does not link to it.
New migrant framing, step by step plus post-arrival checklist. Lower relevance to 417/462 but competes on 'tfn application australia'.

gaps_summary: Our page has no how to apply steps at all; every competitor in the top 5 leads with them. Google reads /tfn as a sales page, not as the answer to 'tax file number working holiday visa'.
No eligibility block (who can apply online, being in Australia, New Zealanders, no-work visa conditions), which is what AI answers quote for 'can I apply from overseas'.
No dated, sourced key figures and no link to the ATO; competitors show 'last updated' dates and official sources.
No 'after your TFN arrives' section, so no natural route to /abn and /superannuation.
FAQ answers run to 60-90 words with service talk mixed in; two contain unsourced timing ('two to four weeks').

changes.where: src/app/(site)/tfn/page.tsx FAQS array (all items) and the FAQ Section
changes.new_text:
Replace FAQS with these ten items, in this order. Answers under 50 words, no blank-line splits needed.
1. Q: 'How do I apply for a TFN on a working holiday visa?' A: 'Once you are in Australia on a 417 or 462 visa, apply online on the ATO website. It is free and you do not send documents. Use your passport details exactly and an Australian address that will still get your post. The ATO says it should arrive within 28 days.'
2. Q: 'Can I apply for a TFN myself, and is it free?' A: 'Yes to both. The ATO application is free. What we do is the work around it: checking your details match your visa record, choosing an address that will still receive the letter, and making sure your employer keeps you off the 45% rate while you wait.'
3. Q: 'Can I apply for a TFN before I arrive in Australia?' A: 'Not on a working holiday visa. The ATO online application is for work rights visa holders who are located in Australia. Have your passport and an Australian postal address ready, and apply after you land.'
4. Q: 'How long does a TFN take to arrive?' A: 'The ATO says you should receive your TFN within 28 days of it receiving a complete application. It comes as a letter to the Australian postal address on your application. Applying a second time during those 28 days can delay it.'
5. Q: 'Can I start work before my TFN arrives?' A: 'Yes. Tell your employer on your TFN declaration that you have applied, and they withhold at the normal rate for 28 days. After that, without your TFN, they must withhold 45% instead of 15%. On $25 an hour that is about $7.50 an hour more.'
6. Q: 'What if my TFN has not arrived after 28 days?' A: 'Do not apply again. Call the ATO on 13 28 61, or +61 2 6216 1111 from overseas, with your receipt ID and passport. They can tell you where it stands and update a wrong address. Tell your employer it is running late.'
7. Q: 'What documents do I need for a TFN?' A: 'For the online application, none to send. The ATO checks your details against your visa, which must be linked to your passport. What matters is that your name, date of birth and passport number match your visa record exactly.'
8. Q: 'I have already been working for weeks without a TFN. Is it too late?' A: 'No. Apply now so the 45% rate stops on future pay. Anything already withheld at 45% is dealt with in your tax return for that financial year, and what comes back depends on your year. Tell us how many weeks were paid at 45%.'
9. Q: 'Do I need a new TFN for a second or third working holiday visa?' A: 'No. A tax file number is issued once and stays with you for life, across a second or third working holiday visa, a change of visa and any time spent outside Australia. If you have lost it, that is a lookup, not a new application.'
10. Q: 'Do I need an ABN as well as a TFN?' A: 'Only if you also work as a contractor or sole trader. A TFN covers employment, where your employer withholds tax for you. An ABN covers contract work, where nothing is withheld for you. You can hold both at the same time.'
Section title stays: 'TFN questions people ask before they message us'.
changes.why: Short, self-contained answers are what Google and AI answers lift. Adds the three questions competitors answer and we do not (how to apply, documents, ABN). Merges the two 'is it free / what am I paying for' items into one honest answer. Removes the unsourced 'most have theirs inside two to four weeks' and the overlong 28 day answer. Adds the ATO 'do not apply twice' rule. faqLd maps FAQS, so the FAQPage schema stays identical to the visible accordion automatically; drop the comment about blank-line splits if no answer uses one.

facts.fact: Online TFN application (Individual Auto-Registration) is for people with a valid work rights visa who are located in Australia; working holiday maker visas 417 and 462 are listed.
No documents need to be sent; the visa must be linked to the passport or travel document.
It is free to apply for a TFN.
You should receive your TFN within 28 days from when the ATO receives your completed application; it is posted to the Australian postal address on the application.
Do not submit another application during the 28 day period, as this can delay processing; after 28 days contact the ATO with your receipt ID.
New Zealanders are automatically granted a work rights visa on arrival in Australia.
Visas with conditions 8101, 8103 or 8116 (no work) cannot use the online application; temporary visitors without a work rights visa use the paper form.
Where a payee has declared they applied for a TFN, the payer withholds at the standard rate for 28 days, then at the top rate if the TFN is still not provided.
Withholding where no TFN is on file for a foreign resident or working holiday maker: 45%.
Working holiday maker rate: 15% on the first $45,000 from the first dollar, no tax-free threshold, effective 1 July 2026.
ATO individual enquiries 13 28 61 (8am to 6pm Mon to Fri); from overseas +61 2 6216 1111 (8am to 5pm AEDT Mon to Fri).
A TFN is issued once and kept for life, across visas.
TFN covers employment with tax withheld; ABN covers contracting with nothing withheld; both can be held.
